title: Aurora MedTech POC kickoff & acceptance criteria
content:
Summary:

This doc captures the kickoff notes, scope, technical approach, workshop agenda, and explicit acceptance criteria for the Aurora MedTech POC. Goal: demonstrate a Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment of Redwood Inference to power clinical note summarization and downstream search, meeting latency, quality, and security requirements necessary for a pilot with 2 hospital customers.

Primary objective:
- Validate that Redwood Private can serve de-identified clinical note summarization reliably within Aurora's network perimeter, with rollup metrics that meet their operational SLOs and clinical QA thresholds.

Background / customer context:
- Aurora MedTech builds clinician-facing summarization and search for post-visit notes. They must keep PHI inside their VPC and require audit logs + KMS integration.
- They have a small GPU on-prem rack (2x A100-ish nodes) and an AWS VPC account for a private control plane.
- Business deadline: internal pilot sign-off by 2026-03-15. This POC is a gating milestone before a 6-month pilot contract.

Scope (what we will deliver in the POC):
- Deploy Redwood Private control plane in Aurora VPC (customer-managed network) + on-prem inference workers in their rack.
- Integrate KMS for key management and enable audit logs streaming to Aurora SIEM.
- Provision model variants: quantized 7B and 13B summarization models (Redwood-verified).
- Implement sample ingestion pipeline for batch historical notes and a streaming route for live summarization from their app.
- Provide a small web-based demo for clinician UAT and a set of automated acceptance tests.

Out-of-scope for this POC:
- Full fine-tuning on customer data (we will test prompt engineering and light evals only).
- Production HA planning beyond the target pilot window.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Aurora: Evelyn Park (technical lead), Dr. Luis Fernandez (clinical sponsor), Maya Li (security/compliance)
- Redwood: Jamie Chen (solutions lead), Aisha Patel (platform engineer), Marco Ruiz (SRE), Samir Kaur (customer success)

Key milestones & timeline (running 8 weeks):
- Week 0 (Kickoff): Align scope, collect network/credentials, schedule workshops.
- Week 1-2: Network setup, private control plane provisioning, KMS integration.
- Week 3: Inference worker install on-prem; model onboarding and kernel tuning.
- Week 4: End-to-end demo with synthetic data; initial latency/throughput tests.
- Week 5: Clinical QA workshop with Aurora clinicians; collect evaluation prompt set.
- Week 6: Acceptance testing (automated + manual).
- Week 7: Buffer and remediation.
- Week 8: Final demo and sign-off.

Success criteria (explicit acceptance tests):
- Security & compliance:
  - Audit logs: All inference requests must produce audit entries sent to Aurora SIEM within 30s (test: replay 500 synthetic requests and verify logs).
  - KMS: Keys are customer-managed and monthly rotation policy validated (test: perform key rotation rehearsal and confirm no loss of access).
  - Data residency: No request payload leaves Aurora VPC (test: network egress verification sampling).

- Reliability & performance:
  - 95th percentile latency for a 512-token summarization request <= 900ms on the 13B quantized variant (measured under steady-state 5 concurrent requests).
  - Throughput: system can sustain 8 concurrent summarization requests per second for sustained 10-minute window without errors >1%.
  - Error budget: maximum of 1% request failures (5xx or timeouts) during acceptance test window.

- Quality (clinical):
  - Rouge-L on held-out clinical test set: >= 0.58 for top-1 summarization outputs using prompt engineering baseline.
  - Clinical accuracy: No clinically-critical hallucination in 95% of 200 sampled notes (reviewed by Dr. Luis Fernandez). Any flagged hallucination must have clear root cause analysis.
  - UAT satisfaction: clinicians score the summaries >=4/5 on usefulness in at least 12 of 15 participants in the workshop.

- Operational & observability:
  - Per-request token-level cost estimate available in console and correlates with measured tokens within 10%.
  - Console dashboards show traceable request -> model -> worker mapping for investigations within <3 clicks.

Acceptance test plan (detailed steps):
1) Security checks: run audit log replay, key rotation, and network egress tests (Aisha + Aurora security lead).
2) Performance sweep: run load generator (10 minutes) per model variant; collect latency percentiles and error rates (Marco).
3) Quality eval: run batch eval on Aurora's withheld note set, produce Rouge and clinical QA spreadsheet (Samir + Dr. Luis).
4) UAT workshop: 90-minute clinician session where participants run live summaries and rate outputs (Jamie facilitates).
5) Final sign-off: joint review meeting with all stakeholders; compare metrics to success criteria and flag remediation items.

Workshop agenda for kickoff (60 minutes):
- 0–10 min: Introductions, goals, quick success criteria readout (Jamie).
- 10–20 min: Aurora infra summary and constraints (Evelyn/Maya).
- 20–35 min: Redwood Private deployment plan and security checklist (Aisha).
- 35–45 min: Model & evaluation plan: variants, prompts, metrics (Samir).
- 45–55 min: Integration points and data flow (Marco).
- 55–60 min: Immediate next steps and action item owners (Jamie).

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: On-prem hardware underperforms expected GPU profile. Mitigation: early hardware benchmark in week 2; fall back to a hybrid mode (burst to dedicated cloud) for comparison and emergency capacity.
- Risk: Clinical QA reveals major hallucinations. Mitigation: freeze model variant, increase conservative decoding settings, add prompt guards and reranker.
- Risk: Networking/VPC firewall blocks control plane communication. Mitigation: SSH jumpbox + temporary port-forward through approved Aurora bastion for initial provisioning; document permanent rules.

Data & access checklist (what we need from Aurora):
- VPC peering details, firewall rules, list of allowed egress endpoints.
- KMS admin contact and test key + rotation schedule.
- Sample de-identified note dataset (2000 notes) plus a withheld test set (200 notes).
- SSO/SAML admin for console access to Aurora testers.

Deliverables at POC close:
- Deployed private control plane + on-prem inference workers documented with runbook.
- Acceptance test report with raw logs, dashboards, and QA spreadsheet.
- Demo recording and clinician workshop notes.
- Proposal for pilot phase with sizing, cost, and SLA options.

Open questions for the kickoff meeting:
- Which model variants should be prioritized if Aurora opts for more aggressive quantization? (13B quantized vs 7B float).
- Nightly data retention policy for logs — 90 days or 365 days? Aurora compliance has a preference but wants recommendation.
- Who will own remediation for any clinical QA issues found (Redwood or Aurora first-pass triage)?

Immediate action items (post-kickoff):
- Aurora: provide VPC diagram and KMS contact by EOD+3 days (Evelyn).
- Redwood: prepare infra deployment runbook and temporary access checklist by EOD+5 days (Aisha + Marco).
- Redwood: prepare prompt baseline and sample eval harness for Aurora review by EOD+7 days (Samir).

Notes to self / internal reminders (informal):
- Keep the initial demo conservative: prioritize no-hallucination behavior over verbosity.
- Bring up quantization and kernel tuning early with serving-runtime team — might need a kernel patch for their unusual sequence length distribution.
- Book clinician workshop in local timezone windows; allow two sessions if scheduling conflicts.

This doc will be iterated during the kickoff. Attachments and logs will be appended to the Confluence page (confluence.redwood/inference/AUR-POC-2025) and Jira SE-4821 will track tasks.

Prepared by: Jamie Chen (Solutions Engineering)
